transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I can plan everything out in detail, but when it’s time to actually sit down and do the work, I just can’t seem to make myself stick with it for more than a few minutes. It's been really frustrating because I want to get my applications done, but I just keep stalling out.
Have you struggled with this difficulty focusing and starting tasks since you were a child, or is this a relatively new change for you?

While it’s been a major struggle with my applications for the past two years, these patterns actually go back to my childhood. Even in elementary school, I would constantly forget my worksheets, leave projects until the last minute, and get report card comments calling me "bright but careless" because I'd skip parts of assignments.
Over the past two years, alongside these focus issues, have you also been experiencing a persistently low mood, low energy, or a loss of interest in things you normally enjoy?

No, I haven't really experienced a persistently low mood, lack of energy, or loss of interest in things. I definitely get highly frustrated and down at times because I can't seem to complete my work and move forward, but my core interest in art history remains really strong.
Do you often experience persistent, uncontrollable worry about various areas of your life, or is your main struggle simply keeping your mind focused and on track?

My main struggle is definitely keeping my mind focused and on track, rather than having uncontrollable anxiety. While I do feel stressed about my lack of progress and the tension with my parents, it's not a constant, generalized worry. Instead, I just face this heavy mental block when trying to start a task, or my mind constantly drifts off to random thoughts.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation (ICD-10: F90.0 / Disturbance of activity and attention). They present with a long-standing, chronic pattern of inattention, including difficulties sustaining attention, initiating and completing tasks, frequent careless mistakes, forgetfulness, and being easily distracted by internal thoughts. These symptoms have been present since childhood (elementary school, well before age 12) and currently cause significant functional impairment in academic/career progress (completing applications) and interpersonal relationships (tension with parents). Depressive and anxiety disorders were ruled out as primary causes.
